items.title: Transportability, calibration, and alert burden of an hourly model for documented continuous vasopressor initiation: a retrospective three-database study.
items.abstract: Clinical prediction models may retain discrimination across settings while losing probability calibration or a workable alert policy. We evaluated this distinction for hourly prediction of documented continuous vasopressor initiation. We used MIMIC-IV v3.1, eICU-CRD v2.0, and SICdb v1.0.8. Untreated adult stays contributed hourly landmarks from ICU hour 6 through 24 while still under observation. The outcome was first initiation within six hours and before ICU/unit exit; exit without initiation remained an operational non-event. Histogram-based gradient boosting (HGB) and logistic regression were fitted and selected in patient-disjoint MIMIC-IV reference-period groups. Evaluation used a separate MIMIC-IV group and two external databases. Source observations were range-checked before predictor summarization; SICdb hourly aggregates were withheld until the source hour had ended. These retrospective timing rules did not verify availability in live clinical information systems. Evaluation included 165,204 landmarks from 9,534 MIMIC-IV reference-period test stays; 2,745,224 landmarks from 168,636 eICU-CRD stays; 58,756 landmarks from 3,997 SICdb stays. HGB AUROCs were 0.770, 0.849, 0.695, respectively. Across 100 identifier-disjoint local-update splits, median Brier skill relative to a calibration-subset constant forecast was -0.168, -0.005, 0.023 before updating and 0.019, 0.025, 0.028 after full logistic recalibration. With thresholds targeting five raw alerts per 100 calibration rows, event detection after six-hour suppression was 0.406, 0.510, 0.275; false emitted alerts were 1.64, 1.52, 1.51 per 100 evaluation rows. Thresholds targeting 80% raw landmark sensitivity detected 0.885, 0.873, 0.883 of eligible events after suppression, while 63.8%, 50.7%, 86.9% of event-free stays received at least one false alert. Discrimination transferred unevenly, while calibration and alert performance remained setting-dependent. The evaluated model and alert policies are not ready for clinical deployment. Offline assessment against prespecified clinical criteria should precede any prospective silent evaluation.

items.title: Frailty and sarcopenia in PeriDialysis-chronic kidney disease: a narrative review of prevalence, prognostic implications, and therapeutic opportunities.
items.abstract: The transition from advanced chronic kidney disease (CKD) to maintenance dialysis is a period of substantial physiological and functional vulnerability. This Review, the peri-dialysis period is defined as the interval from CKD G5 (estimated glomerular filtration rate 2 ) to 3 months after dialysis initiation. Frailty and sarcopenia are common during this transition and may substantially influence treatment tolerance, independence and clinical outcomes. We narratively synthesize evidence on the prevalence, clinical significance, assessment challenges, prognostic implications, and therapeutic opportunities related to frailty and sarcopenia among PeriDialysis CKD patients. Frailty and sarcopenia are overlapping but distinct syndromes. Their development in kidney failure is driven by inflammation, protein-energy wasting, metabolic acidosis, insulin resistance, hormonal disturbances, multimorbidity, inactivity and dialysis-related stressors. Both conditions are associated with higher risks of mortality, hospitalization, functional decline, disability and poorer health-related quality of life. However, substantial heterogeneity exists across diagnostic definitions, assessment tools and measurement timing. Fluid overload and rapid shifts in body water complicate interpretation of body-composition measures, while handgrip strength, gait speed, chair-stand tests and clinician-rated frailty scales offer feasible approaches for routine assessment. Evidence across studies suggests that functional measures are consistently prognostic and may provide complementary or greater prognostic information than muscle mass alone; however, direct head-to-head comparisons are limited and results depend on case definitions and measurement timing. Frailty and sarcopenia should be assessed repeatedly before and after dialysis initiation rather than considered fixed characteristics. A transition-focused, multidisciplinary approach integrating exercise and rehabilitation, individualized nutritional care, symptom and comorbidity management, dialysis optimization and social support may help preserve function and independence.

items.title: Population-based incidence, clinical phenotypes and toxicity-related mortality of immune-related myositis, myocarditis and myasthenia-like overlap (ir-MMM): study.
items.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) often induce immune-related adverse events (irAEs). A potentially fatal irAE is immune-related (ir) myositis and ir-myocarditis, particularly the ir-myositis-myocarditis-myasthenia overlap (ir-MMM). Evidence derives from trials, pharmacovigilance and specialist-centre series, leaving population-based incidence and phenotype-specific risk poorly defined. In a retrospective, population-based cohort, we included all adult patients with cancer treated with ICIs (anti-programmed cell death protein 1/anti-programmed death-ligand 1 and/or anti-cytotoxic T-lymphocyte-associated protein 4) in the Region of Southern Denmark from September 2013 to December 2024. Natural language processing of electronic health records and laboratory data identified potential cases, which were confirmed by expert adjudication. Patients were classified as having isolated ir-myositis, isolated ir-myocarditis or ir-myositis-myocarditis overlap; bulbar/ocular involvement defined ir-MMM. Primary outcomes were phenotype distribution and toxicity-related mortality. Among 2893 ICI-treated patients, 53 (1.8%) developed ir-myositis and/or ir-myocarditis: isolated ir-myositis in 13 of 53 (24%), isolated ir-myocarditis in 12 of 53 (23%), and overlap in 28 of 53 (53%), including 15 (28%) with ir-MMM. Five (9%) died of toxicity, all in the overlap group, and four of five (80%) had ir-MMM. Dyspnoea and bulbar/ocular symptoms were present in 100% and 80% of fatal cases. Median peak high-sensitivity cardiac troponin T (hs-cTnT) was nearly 10-fold higher in fatal (2540 ng/l) than in nonfatal cases (274 ng/l). Isolated ir-myositis caused no deaths but was long-lasting (92% experienced for >6 months). Ir-myositis and/or ir-myocarditis occurred in ∼2% of ICI-treated patients. Mortality was confined to overlap, particularly ir-MMM, and was associated with dyspnoea, bulbar/ocular symptoms and markedly elevated hs-cTnT concentration, features not captured by Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) grading. Our findings support phenotype-based risk stratification over CTCAE grading.
items.journal: ESMO real world data and digital oncology

items.title: Sleep-related worry and its associated factors among shift-work nurses: a cross-sectional study.
items.abstract: Shift work is an inherent characteristic of the nursing profession. Its detrimental effects extend beyond the physiological level, yet the resulting sleep-related worry is often overlooked. This study aimed to assess the level of sleep-related worry among shift-work nurses and identify factors independently associated with it. A cross-sectional survey using convenience sampling was conducted among 326 shift-work nurses from January to March 2026. Data were collected using a General Information Questionnaire, the Anxiety and Preoccupation about Sleep Questionnaire, Athens Insomnia Scale, Social Support Rating Scale, General Self-Efficacy Scale, and Copenhagen Burnout Inventory. Multiple linear regression was employed to determine factors independently associated with sleep-related worry. The total score for sleep-related worry was 35 (28, 41). Spearman correlation analysis indicated that sleep-related worry was positively correlated with insomnia severity ( r  = 0.638, p   r  = 0.519, p   r  = -0.254, p   r  = -0.309, p   β  = 0.449, p   β  = 0.154, p  = 0.007), general self-efficacy ( β  = -0.110, p  = 0.013), and use of sleep medication in the past 6 months ( β  = 0.151, p  < 0.001) were independently associated with sleep-related worry. However, social support was not independently associated with sleep-related worry in the multiple linear regression model. Sleep-related worry among shift-work nurses is at a relatively high level. Interventions addressing self-efficacy, burnout, and sleep health should be incorporated into institutional occupational health policies, alongside legislative measures to protect nurses' psychological health and ensure adequate rest and recovery.

items.title: Intestinal barrier dysfunction and systemic inflammation in adult patients after Fontan operation without protein-losing enteropathy.
items.abstract: Patients after Fontan operation are at risk for multisystemic complications. Chronically elevated central venous pressure and reduced cardiac output may promote intestinal congestion and hypoperfusion, potentially leading to intestinal barrier dysfunction, microbial translocation and systemic inflammation. To investigate biomarkers of intestinal barrier dysfunction and systemic inflammation in adult patients after Fontan operation without protein losing enteropathy (PLE). In this single-center, prospective study adult patients after Fontan operation without PLE and age- and sex-matched healthy controls were enrolled. Intestinal barrier related biomarkers included lipopolysaccharide binding protein (LBP), a marker of endotoxin exposure and host acute phase response, and intestinal fatty-acid binding protein (I-FABP), a marker of enterocyte injury. Systemic inflammation was evaluated using interleukin-6, interleukin-1β, tumor necrosis factor-α, soluble CD14 and C-reactive protein. Twenty-six patients after Fontan operation and thirteen healthy controls were included. There were no differences in age (27 ± 6 vs. 28 ± 4 years, p  = 0.474) or gender (12 (46%) vs. 6 (46%) women, p  = 1.000). Of intestinal barrier dysfunction biomarkers, LBP levels were significantly higher in patients than in healthy controls (median 19.0 (6.9) vs. 12.6 (1.3) ng/mL, p  = 0.038), whereas I-FABP levels were similar (median 1.7 (1.0) vs. 1.5 (0.7) ng/mL, p  = 0.627). All inflammatory biomarkers were significantly elevated in patients after Fontan operation. Adult patients after Fontan operation without PLE showed higher LBP and biomarkers of systemic inflammation, but similar I-FABP, compared to healthy controls. This pattern is consistent with increased endotoxin exposure and low-grade systemic inflammation without evidence of overt enterocyte injury in these complex patients.

items.title: Patient and Physician Preferences in Treating Metastatic Melanoma in the United States: A Discrete Choice Experiment.
items.abstract: Although current National Comprehensive Cancer Network guidelines recommend immunotherapies for advanced melanoma, variability in patients' risk-benefit profiles and treatment characteristics makes treatment selection challenging. Given these differences, we aimed to assess patient and physician preferences for treatment attributes in advanced melanoma. This cross-sectional study included 2 surveys: one administered to patients with self-reported unresectable stage III or IV melanoma and another to treating physicians. A discrete choice experiment (DCE) was used to elicit preferences and the relative importance (RI) of treatment attributes of efficacy (progression-free survival, overall survival [OS], objective response rate), safety (grade 3/4 treatment-related adverse events [TRAEs], endocrine AEs, discontinuation due to TRAEs), and dosing. The DCE included 12 tasks, each with 2 options with varying levels. The same DCE was used across both surveys, with language tailored to each participant group. A hierarchical Bayesian model was used to estimate preference weights for each level. Overall, 75 patients (mean age, 44.8 y; male, 65%) and 75 physicians (mean age, 45.5 y; male, 76%) were included. For both groups, improvement in safety attributes (overall RI, patients: 49%; physicians: 49%) was more important than improvement in efficacy attributes (overall RI, patients: 35%; physicians: 41%). Both groups were willing to accept a decrease in OS from 65% to 55% for a decrease in grade 3/4 TRAEs (60% to 10%) and discontinuation due to TRAEs (40% to 7%), respectively. Endocrine AEs were considered the least important. Patients and physicians prioritized safety over efficacy when efficacy differences were minimal in selecting first-line treatment for advanced melanoma. By eliciting preferences from these groups, this study identifies the treatment attributes most valued by each group and informs patient-centered treatment recommendations and benefit-risk assessment.

items.title: Adaptive immunotherapy dosing in cancer: a structured narrative review and conceptual framework for future clinical investigation.
items.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed cancer treatment, but approved schedules do not establish whether treatment intensity should remain constant as tumor burden, immunity, toxicity, and response evolve. Continued treatment after durable response may add toxicity and treatment burden while providing uncertain incremental benefit. This structured narrative review examines adaptive immunotherapy dosing: prespecified, state-dependent modification of dose, interval, or duration, including interruption and resumption. Exposure-response plateaus and time-varying clearance support investigating alternative regimens but do not establish clinical equivalence. Evidence on discontinuation remains disease- and regimen-specific, precluding generalization from melanoma to non-small cell lung cancer or other settings. Response- and biomarker-guided strategies have prospective support in defined settings, including response-driven adjuvant therapy in melanoma and circulating tumor DNA-selected adjuvant therapy in muscle-invasive bladder cancer. These advances do not validate repeated biomarker-guided adjustment of ICI dose, interval, or duration. Most candidate longitudinal biomarkers show outcome associations without demonstrated utility for dosing adaptation. Artificial intelligence and computational models may integrate serial data but require prospective evaluation, external validation, and safeguards against unsafe individual predictions. Dynamic treatment regimes and adaptive trial methods offer tools for evaluating complete policies, with attention to endpoints, patient preferences, assay performance, equity, and regulation. The proposed conceptual framework organizes these requirements for prospective investigation; it is not a clinical algorithm. Trials must establish whether matching treatment intensity to an evolving clinical state preserves efficacy while reducing toxicity and burden and improving quality of life. Approved regimens and validated disease-specific strategies remain the clinical benchmark.

items.title: Dual immune checkpoint blockade in advanced well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumors, a phase II clinical trial.
items.abstract: Limited options result in objective responses in patients with well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumors (WD-NET). We tested the efficacy of dual immune checkpoint blockade in patients with WD-NET. We planned a phase II clinical trial in patients with WD-NET who progressed within the past 12 months to standard treatments. Patients received ipilimumab 1 mg/kg every 6 weeks and nivolumab 240 mg every 2 weeks for up to 2 years. The primary endpoint was objective response rate (ORR) by RECIST v1.1. Using Simon's 2-stage design, the study planned to accrue 56 patients. This regimen would be considered promising if ORR >15%. Nine patients were enrolled (6 lung, 2 pancreatic, and 1 small bowel). The Mean age was 63.7 years. Four of eight evaluable patients achieved confirmed response (ORR 50%, 95% CI: 16-84). Five of nine patients experienced immune-related toxicity. The trial closed before completing Stage 1 enrollment (9 of 20 planned patients). No formal statistical conclusion could be applied given the incomplete accrual. We observed a higher CD3 infiltration in pre-treatment tumors of patients who had achieved radiological response as compared with those of nonresponders. The combination of ipilimumab and nivolumab in patients with WD-NET results in an observed ORR of 50% in this small clinical trial. These results are hypothesis-generating given the small sample size and premature trial closure. https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT03420521, identifier NCT03420521.

items.title: CXCR2 enhances the migration-independent efficacy of pan-cancer CAR-T cells.
items.abstract: Successful translation of chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cell therapies from hematological cancers to solid cancers has encountered significant hurdles, with a precursory challenge being the infiltration of solid tumors by CAR-T cells. We previously developed a pan-cancer CAR-T cell therapy directed toward the non-functional form of the P2X7 receptor (nfP2X7), an ATP receptor expressed by a diverse range of malignant cells. To enhance trafficking and ostensibly anti-tumor efficacy, we modified these CAR-T cells to express the chemokine receptor CXCR2. When compared to unmodified nfP2X7-targeting CAR-T cells, CXCR2-modified CAR-T cells demonstrated enhanced cancer cell lysis in vitro and improved tumor inhibition in preclinical human prostate and breast tumor xenograft models in vivo . Unexpectedly, improved tumor inhibition occurred independently of CXCR2-driven trafficking to the tumor and was rather associated with enhanced proliferative and cytotoxic capacities. While harnessing the chemokine system to home CAR-T cells into solid tumors has achieved promising outcomes in the field, non-canonical and currently underappreciated roles of chemokine receptors may have contributed to the enhanced efficacy of these modified CAR-T cells. The findings from this study position CXCR2 as a multifaceted and clinically valuable tool which bolsters CAR-T cell anti-tumor efficacy and persistence via mechanisms unrelated to trafficking.

items.title: Case Report: MOGAD presenting as infectious meningoencephalitis with concomitant low-titer GFAP-IgG of uncertain significance.
items.abstract: Myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein (MOG) antibody-associated disease (MOGAD) and autoimmune glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) astrocytopathy (GFAP-A) have recently garnered substantial research interest. Nevertheless, instances of concomitant positivity for MOG-IgG and GFAP-IgG, particularly those presenting as infectious meningoencephalitis, remain rare. This report details the case of a 54-year-old man who presented with headache and fever, with an initial clinical presentation suggestive of infectious meningoencephalitis despite the absence of an identifiable pathogen. Low titers (1:10) of MOG-IgG and GFAP-IgG were detected in both serum and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). MRI of the brain revealed an old post-traumatic encephalomalacic lesion in the right parietal lobe. The patient initially improved with antiviral therapy but subsequently deteriorated, with cognitive decline, visual blurring in the left eye, and bilateral leg weakness. Further testing revealed a marked increase in serum MOG-IgG titer, from 1:10 to 1:320 within one month. A gadolinium-enhanced brain MRI demonstrated new lesions in the brainstem, medial aspects of the bilateral temporal lobes, and the left parietal lobe. Spinal MRI revealed multiple short-segment signal abnormalities in the cervical and thoracic spinal cord, with partial enhancement of the lesions and meninges. Orbital MRI showed edema and thickening of the left optic nerve. The patient was diagnosed with MOGAD, presenting as infectious meningoencephalitis, with concomitant low-titer GFAP-IgG of uncertain significance. The treatment regimen comprised high-dose methylprednisolone and efgartigimod, followed by a tapering course of oral prednisolone and the initiation of rituximab. The patient exhibited symptomatic improvement and sustained remission under combined immunotherapy. This case highlights that MOGAD with concomitant low-titer GFAP-IgG may not initially present its full clinical spectrum. Clinical, radiological, and laboratory features may evolve over time. Therefore, diagnosis should extend beyond the initial presumed etiology, with ongoing reassessment as new evidence emerges.

items.title: Probable Fulminant Meningococcemia with Purpura Fulminans, Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis-Range Mucocutaneous Injury, Hepatitis C, and Bilateral Below-Knee Amputation: A Case Report.
items.abstract: Fulminant meningococcemia can progress within hours to disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) and purpura fulminans, and its skin findings can mimic Stevens-Johnson syndrome/toxic epidermal necrolysis (SJS/TEN). We report a previously healthy 22-year-old man from rural Sindh, Pakistan, with six days of high-grade fever, a purpuric and necrotic eruption with a positive Nikolsky sign, four-site mucosal involvement, and symmetrical acral gangrene. He had severe thrombocytopenia and overt DIC (International Society on Thrombosis and Haemostasis score 5); CT angiography showed patent large vessels with distal microvascular cut-off. Blood cultures obtained after pre-hospital antibiotics were sterile, meningococcal molecular testing was unavailable, and skin biopsy was deferred for bleeding risk, so diagnoses remain clinical. The working diagnosis was probable fulminant meningococcemia with purpura fulminans and presumed drug-induced epidermal necrolysis (35-40% body-surface area), which could not be histologically distinguished from purpura fulminans-associated epidermolysis. Hepatitis C virus infection (RNA 662,053 IU/mL) of suspected injection-associated acquisition was also found. He survived after first-hour empirical ceftriaxone, supportive care, anticoagulation, bilateral below-knee amputation, and sofosbuvir-daclatasvir, but developed a postoperative Pseudomonas aeruginosa stump infection. This probable, unconfirmed case supports first-hour empirical therapy where diagnostics are limited and underscores the need for meningococcal vaccination, injection safety, and evidence-based prescribing.

items.title: Diverging temporal trends and associated factors of adverse birth outcomes among neonates in Guiping, China, 2016-2025: a retrospective study.
items.abstract: Preterm birth (PTB), low birth weight (LBW), macrosomia, and small for gestational age (SGA) are common adverse birth outcomes associated with neonatal morbidity and longer-term health risks. This study examined temporal trends in these outcomes and their associated factors in Guiping, China, from 2016 to 2025. This retrospective study included 49,217 live-born neonates recorded in the maternal and child health information system of Guiping People's Hospital. Joinpoint regression was used to examine temporal trends and estimate annual percent changes (APCs) and average annual percent changes (AAPCs). Multivariable logistic regression was performed to explore factors associated with each outcome, and exploratory Random Forest models were used for supplementary prediction. The prevalence of PTB, LBW, and macrosomia was 10.5%, 10.2%, and 2.0%, respectively, and SGA occurred in 13.6% of eligible singleton live births. In the primary Joinpoint analysis, PTB declined overall (AAPC, -1.68%; 95% CI, -2.45 to -0.91). The APC was positive during 2023-2025 (6.41%; 95% CI, 0.06 to 13.18), but this estimate was based on only three annual observations and did not remain statistically significant when annual errors were assumed to be uncorrelated. SGA also decreased (AAPC, -2.59%; 95% CI, -4.78 to -0.35), while no significant overall trends were found for LBW or macrosomia. In the multivariable analyses, advanced maternal age and multiple gestation were associated with higher odds of PTB and LBW. Second or later birth was associated with lower odds of LBW and SGA but higher odds of macrosomia. Female neonates had higher odds of LBW and lower odds of PTB and macrosomia. Maternal age <20 years and rural residence were associated with higher odds of SGA. PTB, LBW, macrosomia, and SGA followed different temporal patterns between 2016 and 2025. SGA decreased, while LBW and macrosomia showed no significant overall changes. PTB declined early in the study period but increased during 2023-2025 in the primary Joinpoint analysis, although this later increase was not statistically significant when uncorrelated errors were assumed. Further research is needed to assess whether the recent increase in PTB continues.

items.title: Community-based health screening in Madagascar reveals a potential underestimation of non-communicable and infectious disease burden: a cross-sectional study.
items.abstract: To assess the prevalence of selected communicable diseases and cardiometabolic risk factors in adults from underserved inland and coastal communities in Madagascar. A community-based cross-sectional study was conducted in two underserved peripheral communities settings (inland and coastal). Participants underwent standardized health screening, including testing for HIV, hepatitis B and C, and syphilis, as well as measurements of anthropometric parameters, blood pressure, fasting glycemia, and total cholesterol. Descriptive analyses, between-group comparisons, and multivariable logistic regression analyses adjusted for age, sex, and study cohort were performed using Stata version 17, with statistical significance set at p < 0.05. A total of 256 participants (mean age 45.2 ± 17.4 years) were included. HIV infection was detected in 3.1% of participants. Hypertension was present in 28.1%, and elevated fasting glycemia (≥ 7 mmol/L) in 15.6%. The prevalence of HIV, hepatitis C, and syphilis was significantly higher in the coastal community, which also showed a higher proportion of elevated total cholesterol. After adjustment for age and sex, elevated total cholesterol remained the only cardiometabolic indicator independently associated with the coastal community. This study demonstrates the feasibility and value of integrated community-based health screening in underserved communities in Madagascar. The findings indicate a considerable burden of both communicable diseases and cardiometabolic risk factors and reveal important geographical differences between inland and coastal communities. Although not nationally representative, the results provide valuable contemporary epidemiological data and support the expansion of integrated community-based surveillance and preventive health programmes in resource-limited settings.

items.title: Anaemia in pregnancy at booking: prevalence, risk factors and perinatal outcomes among antenatal clinic attendees in a secondary healthcare facility in North Central Nigeria: an analytical study.
items.abstract: Anaemia during pregnancy is an unacceptable public health problem in most developing countries inclusive of Nigeria where access to adequate nutrition and quality healthcare services is limited. To determine the prevalence and severity of anaemia, associated socio-demographic, clinical, and obstetric factors, and perinatal outcomes among women presenting for antenatal booking at a secondary health facility in North-Central Nigeria. This analytical cross-sectional study enrolled 1,141 consecutive eligible pregnant women who presented for antenatal booking at a secondary healthcare facility in North-Central Nigeria, between 14 October 2022 and 14 October 2023. Written informed consent was obtained from all participants before enrolment. Data were collected using a pre-tested interviewer administered questionnaire. Packed cell volume (PCV) was determined using the microhaematocrit method, and haemoglobin concentration was estimated by dividing the PCV by three. Anaemia at booking was defined according to World Health Organization (WHO) criteria. Women diagnosed with anaemia underwent further laboratory investigations to determine the underlying aetiology and appropriate management was instituted according to the identified aetiology and hospital protocol. All participants received routine haematinics supplementation and were followed prospectively through delivery to capture perinatal outcomes. Data were analyzed using SPSS version 24 and associations were assessed using Chi-square tests, while multivariable logistic regression identified independent predictors of anaemia at booking; extremely high odds ratios were verified for sparse-data bias and collinearity and p ≤ 0.05 was considered statistically significant. Anaemia at booking was present in 728 (63.8%) pregnant women, with microcytic hypochromic anaemia accounting for 56.4% of cases. Socio demographic characteristics significantly associated with anaemia at booking were: occupation (p < 0.001), religion (p < 0.001), level of education (p = 0.001), social class (p < 0.001) and low women's dietary diversity score (WDDS) (p < 0.001). Significant obstetric and clinical factors were: gravidity (p < 0.001), history of miscarriage (p = 0.001), number of living children (p < 0.001), history of pre conceptional counselling and care (p < 0.001), use of herbal medications (p < 0.001), substance abuse (p = 0.001), non-use of insecticide-treated nets (p < 0.001), and prior haematinic use (p < 0.001). Laboratory parameters showed that hookworm infestation, Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) infection, hepatitis B and C virus infections, and malaria parasitaemia all had significant relationship (all p < 0.001) with anaemia at booking. Packed cell volume improved significantly twelve weeks following treatment (p < 0.001). Adverse perinatal outcomes documented were: intrauterine fetal death, intrauterine growth restriction, miscarriage, low birth weight, perinatal asphyxia, and preterm delivery (p < 0.001). After adjustment for potential confounders, independent predictors of anaemia at booking were hookworm infestation (AOR = 7.99, 95% CI: 4.00-15.95), HIV infection (AOR = 8.37, 95% CI: 2.58-27.17), malaria parasitaemia (AOR = 139.31, 95% CI: 64.82-299.07), non-use of insecticide treated nets (AOR = 5.98, 95% CI: 2.72-13.14), substance abuse (AOR = 1.75, 95% CI: 1.25-2.44), and low WDDS (AOR = 43.45, 95% CI: 29.91-63.11). Anaemia at booking remains highly prevalent and is associated with adverse perinatal outcomes. The findings highlight a persistent gap between existing antenatal care guideline recommendations and their implementation in routine clinical practice. Therefore, strengthening implementation of existing antenatal care guidelines, including nutritional interventions, infection control, early screening and treatment, and preconception care, could substantially reduce the burden of maternal anaemia and improve pregnancy outcomes.

items.title: TIM-3 blockade exacerbates intestinal ischemia-reperfusion injury and alters macrophage polarization.
items.abstract: ObjectiveIntestinal ischemia-reperfusion injury is a critical condition associated with a high mortality rate. T-cell immunoglobulin and mucin domain-containing protein 3 (TIM-3), a protein expressed on T cells and innate immune cells, plays regulatory roles in inflammatory diseases. However, the role of TIM-3 in modulating immune responses during intestinal ischemia-reperfusion injury remains unclear.MethodsIn the present study, C57BL/6 mice were subjected to intestinal ischemia-reperfusion injury by occlusion of the superior mesenteric artery and were administered anti-TIM-3 monoclonal antibodies to block intestinal TIM-3 function.ResultsTIM-3 expression increased significantly following intestinal ischemia-reperfusion, and this increase was associated with the expression of inflammatory cytokines. Despite this association, functional blockade of TIM-3 using anti-TIM-3 monoclonal antibodies exacerbated intestinal damage and inflammatory responses compared with those in control mice. Moreover, intestinal ischemia-reperfusion injury increased the infiltration of M1 and M2 macrophages, whereas TIM-3 inhibition promoted the conversion of M2 macrophages to M1 macrophages. This transformation was associated with increased Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) expression and decreased levels of intestinal phosphorylated signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (STAT3) and Akt.ConclusionOverall, TIM-3 modulates macrophage polarization through the TLR4/STAT3/Akt signaling pathway, thereby alleviating inflammation and tissue damage during intestinal ischemia-reperfusion injury. These findings suggest that TIM-3 serves as a therapeutic target for managing intestinal ischemia-reperfusion injury.
items.journal: The Journal of international medical research

items.title: Comparison of Perioperative Remimazolam and Propofol for Short-Term Postoperative Fatigue Syndrome After Laparoscopic Liver Cancer Resection.
items.abstract: To compare the effects of perioperative remimazolam and propofol for anesthesia induction and maintenance on short-term postoperative fatigue syndrome (POFS) in patients undergoing laparoscopic liver cancer resection. In this single-centre, randomised, single-blind study. Ninety-two patients aged 18-65 years (BMI 18-28 kg/m 2 ; ASA I-III) scheduled for elective laparoscopic liver cancer resection (January 2025-August 2025) were randomly assigned to the remimazolam group (Group R, n=46) or propofol group (Group P, n=46). Group R received remimazolam 0.2 mg/kg for induction and 0.4-1.2 mg/kg/h for maintenance; Group P received propofol 1.5-2.0 mg/kg for induction and 4-6 mg/kg/h for maintenance. Other anesthetic management was identical. Heart rate, mean arterial pressure, and oxygen saturation were recorded at predefined perioperative time points. Pain (VAS), fatigue (Christensen Postoperative Fatigue Scale), and recovery quality (QoR-15) were assessed preoperatively (D0) and on postoperative days 1 (D1) and 3 (D3). Recovery and sedation (Riker SAS) were also evaluated. VAS scores did not differ between groups at D0, D1, or D3 (P>0.05). Baseline fatigue scores were comparable, but Group R had significantly lower fatigue scores at D1 and D3 (P<0.05). QoR-15 scores were higher in Group R on D1 (P<0.05) but similar at D3. Recovery time, extubation time, and PACU stay were comparable. No serious adverse events or intraoperative awareness occurred. Intraoperative hypotension and sinus bradycardia were less frequent in Group R (P<0.05). Postoperative complications were similar between groups. Perioperative remimazolam reduces short-term POFS severity and enhances early postoperative recovery compared with propofol. Many people feel very tired after liver cancer surgery. This short-term postoperative fatigue can slow recovery, delay movement, and reduce quality of life. Doctors believe that the type of anaesthesia used during surgery may influence how tired patients feel afterward. However, not very much is known about how different anaesthetic drugs affect this early fatigue. In this study, we compared two commonly used anaesthetics—remimazolam and propofol—in adults undergoing laparoscopic liver cancer surgery. We randomly assigned 92 patients to receive one of the two drugs during surgery. We then measured their pain, fatigue levels, recovery quality, and any side effects during the first three days after surgery. Patients who received remimazolam reported less fatigue and better overall recovery on the first day after surgery. They also experienced fewer episodes of low blood pressure and slow heart rate during the operation. Pain levels and overall complication rates were similar between groups. These results suggest that choosing remimazolam may help reduce early postoperative fatigue and support smoother recovery after liver cancer surgery.

items.title: Detection of hypovascular colorectal liver metastases with photon-counting detector CT versus energy-integrating detector CT: a blinded intra-patient comparison of routine clinical protocols using an MRI-anchored reference standard.
items.abstract: Contrast-enhanced CT remains the staging workhorse in metastatic colorectal cancer but under-detects small hypovascular colorectal liver metastases (CRLM) relative to MRI. Photon-counting detector CT (PCCT) offers higher spatial resolution and lower electronic noise, yet clinical evidence on lesion detection is scarce. In this single-centre, intra-patient reader study, 15 patients with colorectal cancer and hepatic metastases underwent both energy-integrating detector CT (EID-CT) and PCCT within the same month with each scanner's routine protocol (PCCT: 140 kV, 0.4 mm sections; EID-CT: 100 kV, 1.0 mm sections), during documented oncological stability, plus contrast-enhanced liver MRI. A consensus panel defined an MRI-anchored reference map of 46 metastases. Three radiologists of differing experience independently reviewed both arms in randomised order, blinded to scanner type, clinical data and reference standard, without cue to lesion number or location. Detection, conspicuity and diagnostic confidence were scored per reference lesion. PCCT was read at conventional-equivalent monoenergies (65-70 keV). Per-lesion sensitivity against the MRI-anchored reference was 138/138 reads (100%; 95% CI 97.3-100) for PCCT versus 122/138 (88.4%; 95% CI 82.0-92.7) for EID-CT; all 16 discordant reads favoured PCCT (exact McNemar P < 0.001; patient-clustered bootstrap difference +11.5 points, 95% CI 1.6-24.1). Eight of 46 metastases (17.4%) were missed on EID-CT and none on PCCT. The complete metastatic burden was reproduced in 45/45 patient-level PCCT reads versus 37/45 (82.2%) on EID-CT. Composite conspicuity was 4.57 ± 0.48 versus 3.53 ± 0.88 (+1.04, patient-clustered 95% CI 0.72-1.33; P < 0.001) and diagnostic confidence 4.28 ± 0.53 versus 3.62 ± 0.87 (+0.66, 95% CI 0.42-0.89; P < 0.001). The confidence gain was smaller for the least experienced reader (mixed-effects model P = 0.004). False-positive findings were not recorded, so specificity could not be assessed. In this preliminary comparison of two routine clinical protocols, PCCT showed higher per-lesion sensitivity than EID-CT, identifying every reference metastasis, and improved conspicuity and confidence, even without low-keV optimisation. Because section thickness, tube voltage, pitch and kernel differed between protocols, the advantage reflects the PCCT system as a whole rather than the detector alone. PCCT may narrow the CT-MRI detection gap in CRLM, a hypothesis requiring confirmation in larger free-response studies with matched reconstruction parameters.

items.title: Clinically undetected malignancies in deceased organ and tissue donors: solid organ recipient outcomes and cryopreserved tissue discard.
items.abstract: Unexpected donor malignancy creates uncertainty for solid organ recipients and affects tissue release decisions. We retrospectively reviewed two tissue donor cohorts in Czechia during 2021-2025: 78 vascular and 57 musculoskeletal donors, with one donor contributing to both cohorts, giving 134 unique donors. Malignancy was identified in 1/78 vascular donors (1.28%; pancreatic adenocarcinoma) and 3/57 musculoskeletal donors (5.26%; two prostate adenocarcinomas and one papillary thyroid carcinoma). Pancreatic cancer was diagnosed on definitive sections from an intraoperative biopsy; the other cancers were identified at autopsy. Three affected donors provided six kidneys and one liver to seven recipients. Transplant-center reports of routine clinical follow-up documented no donor-transmitted malignancy during 14-39 months of available follow-up. Six recipients were alive with functioning grafts; one kidney recipient died from sepsis at 14 months. No tissue from the four affected donors was released for clinical use: 14 processed grafts and 19 unprocessed tissue collections were discarded. Histopathology detected the donor cancers; quarantine and final release checks within the quality management system (QMS) prevented tissue release in all four cases. These observations do not establish equivalent transmission risks across tumor types, exclude later transmission, or quantify the sensitivity or overall effectiveness of the QMS.

items.title: Commentary: Hepatic immune microenvironment dynamics in severe obesity and post-bariatric surgery: insights from immunohistochemical analysis.
Synthesis, preclinical evaluation, and the first-in-human study of [ 18 F]AlF-NOTA-FZSR for neuroendocrine neoplasms compared with [ 68 Ga]Ga-DOTA-NOC and [ 68 Ga]Ga-DOTA-TATE.
items.abstract: To improve the detection of neuroendocrine neoplasms (NENs), we developed a series of octreotide-based somatostatin receptor (SSTR)-targeted probes and sought to identify an optimal candidate through preclinical and clinical head-to-head evaluation versus [ 68 Ga]Ga-DOTA-TATE and [ 68 Ga]Ga-DOTA-NOC. Eight original probes were synthesised and radiolabelled with 68 Ga or 18 F. The in vitro stability of the probes in saline and human serum, as well as their in vivo stability through urine sampling, was determined by radio-high-performance liquid chromatography (radio-HPLC). Micro-PET/CT imaging was performed in AR42J xenograft-bearing mice 60 min after injection of the radiotracers via the tail vein. On the basis of preclinical screening, [ 18 F]AlF-NOTA-FZSR was selected for clinical PET/CT and directly compared with [ 68 Ga]Ga-DOTA-TATE and [ 68 Ga]Ga-DOTA-NOC in patients with NENs. All probes were successfully synthesised and radiolabelled with high radiochemical purity (> 98%) and showed good in vitro and in vivo stability (> 95% for 2 h). Among them, [ 18 F]AlF-NOTA-FZSR demonstrated the highest tumour uptake on micro-PET/CT in the AR42J model (41.17 ± 2.50%ID/g at 60 min), exceeding that of [ 68 Ga]Ga-DOTA-NOC (29.67 ± 1.53%ID/g) and [ 68 Ga]Ga-DOTA-TATE (11.2 ± 1.13%ID/g). In clinical PET/CT studies, [ 18 F]AlF-NOTA-FZSR detected lesions not identified by either [ 68 Ga]Ga-DOTA-NOC or [ 68 Ga]Ga-DOTA-TATE. In a patient with liver metastases, [ 18 F]AlF-NOTA-FZSR showed higher lesion uptake than [ 68 Ga]Ga-DOTA-TATE at both early and delayed imaging. At the early imaging time point (45-60 min post-injection), the SUVmax values of [ 68 Ga]Ga-DOTA-TATE and [ 18 F]AlF-NOTA-FZSR were 8.3 and 8.9, respectively. A delayed scan was performed approximately 30 min after the initial imaging session, the corresponding SUVmax values were 10.6 and 8.8, respectively, with a liver background SUVmax of 6.9. In a patient with metastatic pulmonary neuroendocrine carcinoma, [ 18 F]AlF-NOTA-FZSR (SUVmax = 13.6 for rib, SUVmax = 9.1 for thoracic vertebrae) also demonstrated markedly greater sensitivity than [ 68 Ga]Ga-DOTA-NOC (SUVmax = 1.4 for rib, SUVmax = 1.8 for thoracic vertebrae) for detecting bone metastases. We developed several novel SSTR-targeted probes with favourable physicochemical properties and identified [ 18 F]AlF-NOTA-FZSR as the most promising candidate. Compared with [ 68 Ga]Ga-DOTA-TATE and [ 68 Ga]Ga-DOTA-NOC, [ 18 F]AlF-NOTA-FZSR showed superior lesion detection in patients with NENs, supporting its potential for clinical translation.
